newsitem.title: UK: Pemex eyes $250 mln 5-year bond this week - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Pemex eyes $250 mln 5-year bond this week - dealers.

text.p: Mexico's state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) could launch a $250 million five-year Eurobond as early as this week, new issues traders said on Tuesday.
"The Pemex deal, a $250 million five-year issue, could come this week," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.
SBC Warburg was tipped as lead manager, but officials there declined to comment. Spread talk was around 155 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, dealers said.
"The indicated spread (155 b.p.) looks very expensive. We would prefer to see a Pemex deal closer to 200 b.p. over," the European bank official said.

Earlier this month, Pemex officials said it planned to place three debt issues totalling $800 million in 1997. Pemex was eyeing both the Italian lira and dollar sectors, its corporate finance director said.
Last October Pemex launched a $300 million three-year Eurobond at 175 b.p. over Treasuries. Pemex is rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB by Standard & Poor's.
